Excerpts from Khawaja's upcoming autobiography, Sabr, published by the Sydney Morning Herald (SMH) on Saturday, suggested that the controversial practice was not restricted to the third Test in Cape Town but had also been attempted in the preceding match. The revelations have triggered strong reactions, with former Australia coach Darren Lehmann rejecting Khawaja's claims and ex-England captain Michael Vaughan also expressing his displeasure. Together, as a team, we need to take that collectively. That is all,” the former Australian batter said. However, Khawaja stopped short of retracting his assertion that the players knew about the ball-tampering episode. “But now that everyone’s talking, am I going to deny that everyone knew? Nah. item.title: Fran Gonzalez explains his decision to leave Real Madrid – “You have other dreams”
item.description: Fran Gonzalez explains his decision to leave Real Madrid – “You have other dreams” Fran Gonzalez was one of the less talked-about exits for Real Madrid in a summer that was saw a lot of action. The young goalkeeper, after multiple years with the club’s academy, left Real Madrid to join Sevilla on a deal worth €3 million . Although Gonzalez has yet to make a breakthrough at Sevilla, he has recently explained his decision to leave Real Madrid in the summer in great detail. Gonzalez on leaving Real Madrid Fran Gonzalez only ever featured in one game for Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) When asked about his decision to leave the Spanish capital, Gonzalez pointed some key reasons including the desire to make it elsewhere. “I had closed a chapter there in Madrid, with Castilla, and I believed the best thing for me was to take that leap, wherever it might be,” he said (h/t Diario AS ). “Obviously, it’s normal for young goalkeepers not to play right away, no matter where they go, because I come from the Primera RFEF, a competition that has improved a lot in recent years, but it’s a big step. I feel very prepared to make that leap,” he added. Gonzalez explained he had felt his time at Real Madrid academy had come to an end and it was time for a new challenge elsewhere. “I felt that I had finished a stage, and Sevilla is one of the great clubs in Spain, a truly historic club, very good in every sense, and a real opportunity for me to compete and play in the coming years, ” he said. Gonzalez on joining Sevilla Fran Gonzalez spent multiple years at La Fabrica . (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Gonzalez admitted it was quite painful to leave Valdebebas, as he hailed Real Madrid as the best club in the world. However, the goalkeeper admitted it was his desire to join Sevilla and that he was drawn to the opportunity. “It’s not easy to leave what is probably the best club in the world, but well, many times you have other dreams and my dream was to come to Sevilla, from the first moment I was very clear about it. “I didn’t even have to think about it, it’s a place to continue growing and to be able to stay for a long time ,” he concluded. Gonzalez’s spell at Sevilla, though, has started off slowly, with his only appearance this season coming in Copa Del Rey. He is still comfortably behind Odysseas Vlachodimos in the pecking order. However, the young Spaniard is confident he can soon fight for a place in the first-team and is ready to exercise patience.

The Catalan leaders are currently two points clear of the Rojiblancos, who can move top with a win over a side they knocked out of the Champions League and Copa del Rey last season. item.title: ‘I’m Going to Ignore It,’ ‘You’ve Gotta Have Some Credibility’ — NFL Insider Refuses to Back Dianna Russini’s Reporting After Mike Vrabel Scandal
item.description: Former NFL reporter Dianna Russini and New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. Returning to NFL reporting after a public controversy is difficult enough, but rebuilding trust with fellow insiders may be an even bigger challenge for Dianna Russini. Her rumored plans to return to sports media have already drawn a firm response from Pro Football Talk founder Mike Florio, who says he will not pass along her future reports without independent confirmation, leaving Russini with a serious question to address before making her comeback. Mike Florio Challenges Dianna Russini to Restore Her Credibility Florio explained his position during an appearance on “PFT Live,” where he questioned whether Russini could regain the credibility needed to work as an NFL insider. He said his role involves sharing and validating reports from other journalists, but he cannot do that when he does not trust the original source. “If there’s going to be actual reporting as part of this, you’ve gotta have some credibility, or nobody’s going to believe what you say,” Florio said . “Is there going to be an effort to be an insider again?” He made it clear that Russini’s previous explanations have not changed his position. Florio said he would not amplify her work unless another reporter without similar credibility concerns independently confirmed the information. “After everything that’s happened, everything we know, I’m not going to be inclined to believe anything. Which means I’m not going to be amplifying anything,” Florio said. “I don’t care what the reporting is. Unless and until it’s confirmed by someone who doesn’t have these credibility issues, I’m going to ignore it. Unless the credibility is somehow restored.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor The dispute traces back to April, when Page Six published photographs of Russini and New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel together at a resort in Sedona, Arizona. The images showed the two hugging and holding hands. Both were married to other people at the time. Russini and The Athletic initially described the meeting as a coincidental gathering involving a larger group. However, reports later surfaced about previous encounters, including a boat outing in Tennessee in 2021. Russini resigned from The Athletic on April 14 while denying a romantic relationship with Vrabel. A subsequent five-month internal review examined more than 900 stories, videos, and podcasts. The investigation found that her undisclosed relationship violated newsroom standards, although it found no definitive evidence that she directly biased coverage to benefit Vrabel’s teams. item.description: Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) looks to pass during the first half against the Missouri Tigers at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium. (William Purnell-Imagn Images) The SEC has explained why replays let the fumble call on Arch Manning’s third-quarter throw stand. The ruling kept alive the drive that started No. 7 Texas on a run of 21 straight points in a 34-20 win at No. 18 Missouri. Manning was hit on his arm as he tried to throw on third-and-10. Officials ruled it a fumble that Texas recovered for a first down, and the call stood after review. However, the league’s explanation didn’t satisfy a number of critics, one of whom pointed to an official’s signal on the play, while Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz chose not to blame the officials to avoid paying a hefty fine. How the Arch Manning Fumble Unfolded and What the Rulebook Says Texas trailed 20-13 and faced third-and-10 at the Missouri 39 with 2:22 left in the third quarter when Tigers linebacker Brian Huff caught Manning’s right arm as he tried to throw. The ball came loose, sailed forward and landed downfield, where no Missouri defender got to it. Texas receiver Emmett Mosley V scooped it up at the Missouri 25, four yards past the line to gain, and officials ruled it a fumble recovered by Texas. The ruling held up on replay, which spared Texas a fourth-and-10 at the Missouri 39 and served the Longhorns a fresh set of downs on a silver platter. Three plays later, Manning hit Jermaine Bishop Jr. for a 25-yard touchdown to tie the game at 20, and the Longhorns took their first lead of the day on his 23-yard scoring pass to Raleek Brown with 5:03 to play. The SEC laid out its reasoning in a statement after the game. “The ruling on the field was a fumble. In replay review, it was determined there was no clear and obvious video evidence that he had firm control of the ball when the hand intentionally started forward in order to overturn the call.” That explanation leans on the wording of college football’s rulebook, which reads, “When a Team A player is holding the ball to pass it forward toward the neutral zone, any intentional forward movement of the passer’s hand with the ball firmly in their control starts the forward pass unless the player clearly starts to bring the ball back with firm control to the passer’s body. “If a Team B player contacts the passer or ball after forward movement begins and the ball leaves the passer’s hand, a forward pass is ruled regardless of where the ball strikes the ground or a player.” Critics Push Back as Eli Drinkwitz Steers Clear of Blaming the Officials The statement also left one thing unaddressed. Will Mohammed Siraj play the 3rd ODI vs New Zealand in Hamilton? India already hold a 2-0 lead in the five-match series, and the pressure on the visitors is therefore a good deal lower than it was at the start of the tour. The advantage was secured in Wellington on 7 November, where rain ended the second ODI, and India were declared winners by four runs under the DLS method. They had been 113 for 7 after 26 overs, chasing a modest target after bowling New Zealand out for 134, and it was left to the weather to settle the result in their favour. Gurnoor Brar was the star with career-best figures of 4 for 30, while Auqib Nabi, Anshul Kamboj and Axar Patel took two wickets each. The batting was less convincing, with Shubman Gill out for a duck, Virat Kohli making 7 and Axar Patel 7, although Shreyas Iyer (30) and KL Rahul (26 not out) did enough to take India close to the par score. item.title: Richie Incognito makes feelings clear on Maxx Crosby trade as Cowboys rumors resurface
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images Richie Incognito has made it clear he does not want the Las Vegas Raiders to trade Maxx Crosby, despite fresh speculation linking the defensive end with the Dallas Cowboys. The former Raiders offensive lineman believes Crosby remains the team’s most valuable player and has questioned whether any potential offer would justify moving him. Crosby’s future has been discussed since the end of last season, when frustration over his placement on injured reserve following a knee injury reportedly brought his time in Las Vegas close to an end. The Raiders nearly traded him to the Baltimore Ravens, who agreed to send two first-round picks before Crosby failed his physical and the deal collapsed. Richie Incognito strongly opposes Las Vegas Raiders trading Maxx Crosby Speaking on the Initial Contact podcast, Incognito acknowledged that the trade market for elite players has become difficult to judge. However, he made his own position on Crosby’s future clear. “Trading Max, I absolutely hate the idea, but he is our most valuable piece,” Incognito said. He also questioned whether the Raiders would receive the kind of compensation needed to part with their star pass-rusher. Incognito pointed to the Chicago Bears giving up two first-round picks for Jeffrey Simmons, while suggesting there is a significant gap between valuations across the market. The Cowboys have remained part of the conversation after previously making three offers for Crosby. Dallas were reportedly only willing to part with one first-round pick, unlike Baltimore’s proposed package. However, Crosby has made his own preference clear. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that the defensive end does not want to leave Las Vegas and hopes to remain a Raider for life. Crosby has also publicly reiterated his commitment to the franchise, saying: “I love being a Raider. I’ve said that about a million times; this is where I want to be.” There is still a reason the trade speculation has not disappeared. Tom Pelissero raised the question of whether Crosby could command two first-round picks after Simmons, who is also 29, received that level of compensation. Crosby has recorded 461 tackles and 72.5 sacks in his career, compared with Simmons’ 420 tackles and 47.5 sacks. This season, he has 22 tackles, three sacks, a forced fumble, a fumble recovery and a pass defended. With the trade deadline approaching, the Raiders face continued questions about their most valuable defensive asset. For Incognito, though, the answer is simple: keeping Crosby should remain the priority. item.description: Usman Khawaja made his Test debut for Australia against England in 2011 [Getty Images] Usman Khawaja said he has "not thrown anyone under the bus" with revelations about the sandpaper scandal that engulfed the Australia team in 2018. In his autobiography - Sabr - and in an interview with the Sydney Morning Herald, Khawaja claimed the entire team should take responsibility for the plot to use sandpaper on the ball in the third Test against South Africa eight years ago. At the time, the only players punished were captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and opener Cameron Bancroft. Speaking in videos posted on Instagram on Sunday to clarify his comments, Khawaja said: "You would have seen when I mentioned it was all of us, that's implying that whether we like it or not, we are all responsible for what happened together. "As a team, we need to take that collectively. That is all. "But now that everyone's talking, am I going to deny that everyone knew? Nah, I won't deny that, either. But I never speak on behalf of anyone else in my book, contrary to what the headlines in clickbait media would have you think." Other players involved in the Cape Town controversy have repeatedly denied involvement or knowledge of the plot to alter the condition of the ball by rubbing it with sandpaper. Four bowlers who played for Australia in that Test - Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon - remain part of the team. Cummins has been Test captain since 2021. In 2021, the quartet released a joint statement which said they "did not know a foreign substance was taken on to the field". On Saturday, Darren Lehmann, the Australia coach who resigned in the wake of the ball-tampering scandal, also denied Khawaja's claims when he told ABC: "I don't think everyone would have known." Khawaja retired from international cricket in January. He scored 6,229 runs in 88 Tests for Australia. In October, it was revealed that Khawaja had met with Cummins to discuss the contents of the upcoming autobiography. That meeting took place before Australia's recent Test series in South Africa, which the Proteas won 2-1. In the videos on Instagram, 39-year-old Khawaja explained that blame for the plot should have been shared among the entire set-up, not only Smith, Warner and Bancroft.
